1 big thing: Axios is seeking an execution-focused Director of Accounting to lead accounting operations, monthly close, treasury, tax, audit, compliance, and finance systems as our business and finance function continues to scale.

Why it matters: Strong accounting operations create the foundation for faster, clearer, and more reliable business decisions. This role will help ensure our financials are accurate, audit-ready, and built to support continued growth.

Go deeper: This role sits on our Finance team, manages one direct report, and partners closely with FP&A, Payroll, Revenue Finance, department leaders, and external partners.

Responsibilities include:

  • Lead the monthly close process, including close timelines, journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, fixed assets, and close reporting packages.
  • Maintain accounting policies, procedures, controls, chart of accounts governance, and operational documentation to support accurate and scalable financial reporting.
  • Oversee AP, procurement, vendor management, contractor payments, cash management, bank reconciliations, 13-week cash forecasting, and treasury operations.
  • Manage bank access, fraud prevention, and accounting control processes to ensure strong financial governance and compliance.
  • Partner with Finance leadership to improve cash visibility, working capital management, and accounting operations.
  • Lead external audit coordination and oversee tax, sales and use tax, and related compliance processes with external partners.
  • Own and improve accounting systems, integrations, workflows, data integrity, SOPs, and business continuity documentation across finance operations.
  • Drive automation, AI adoption, and process improvements to improve efficiency, scalability, accuracy, and controls.
  • Partner cross-functionally with FP&A, Payroll, Revenue Finance, and business leaders to support forecasting, reporting, and operational decision-making.
  • Lead, coach, and develop accounting team members while fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture.

The details: Ideal candidates will demonstrate most of the following:

  • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of month-end close, audit, tax, treasury, internal controls, and accounting operations.
  • Strong knowledge of GAAP, accrual accounting, balance sheet management, AP, cash management, and financial reporting.
  • Experience managing accounting operations in a fast-paced, scaling organization.
  • Experience with ERP systems and finance process automation; Sage Intacct experience preferred.
  • Experience leading audits and managing relationships with external tax and accounting advisors.
  • Familiarity with sales and use tax, state filings, nexus considerations, and compliance workflows.
  • Strong analytical, project management, and process improvement skills, including leveraging systems, automation, AI, and workflow redesign to improve accounting operations.
  • Advanced Excel and Google Sheets proficiency.
  • Strong communication, cross-functional partnership, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience managing and developing team members.
  • High-accountability, execution-oriented mindset with comfort operating in a fast-paced environment.

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $145,000 - $185,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.

What Axios brings to the table besides salary:

  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Robust PPO and High Deductible health insurance options on the Blue Cross Blue Shield network
  • Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution for the high deductible health plan option
  • Dental and vision coverage
  • Primary caregiver 12-week paid leave
  • Birth-givers will have an additional 6-8 weeks depending on type of delivery, for a total of 18-20 weeks continuous leave
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays
  • One mental health day per quarter
  • Annual learning and development stipend
  • $100 monthly work-from-home stipend
  • Tele-mental health services through Headspace
  • OneMedical membership, including tele-health services
  • Personal health advocacy resources through HealthAdvocate
  • Inclusive fertility, hormonal health and family forming benefits through Carrot Fertility
  • Access to the Axios “Family Fund”, which was created to allow employees to request financial support when facing financial hardship or emergencies
  • Increased work flexibility for parents and caretakers
  • Virtual company-sponsored social events
  • A strong and positive work environment
  • A commitment to an open, inclusive, and diverse work culture

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement

Axios is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. raw.description:
About Radformation

Radformation is transforming the way cancer clinics deliver care. Our innovative software automates and standardizes radiation oncology workflows, enabling clinicians to plan and deliver treatments faster, safer, and more consistently, so patients everywhere can receive the same high-quality care.

Our software focuses on three key areas:

  • Time savings through automation
  • Error reduction through automated systems
  • Increased quality care through advanced algorithms and workflows

We are a fully remote, mission-driven team united by a shared goal: to reduce cancer’s global impact and help save more of the 10 million lives it claims each year. Every line of code, every product release, and every conversation with our customers brings us closer to ensuring no patient’s treatment quality depends on where they live.

Why This Role Matters

ClearCalc is a vendor-agnostic independent calculation software platform for treatment planning second checks, helping radiation oncology clinics improve quality, consistency, and confidence in patient treatment plans.

As a QA Manager, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality and reliability of ClearCalc before it reaches customers. Working closely with Product Management, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Customer Success teams, you will test new product releases, investigate and resolve issues, support customer troubleshooting efforts, and contribute to medical device documentation activities.

This role requires a strong understanding of radiation oncology quality assurance principles and clinical workflows. Your expertise will help drive product quality, support regulatory compliance, and ultimately improve efficiency and patient care for clinics around the world. The ideal candidate is passionate about radiation therapy, enjoys learning new technologies, and thrives in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. They bring strong organizational and communication skills, excel at managing multiple priorities, and are motivated by helping clinicians deliver the highest quality care possible.

Responsibilities Include

  • Testing product versions prior to release to aid in quality assurance using C# in Visual Studio.
  • Version verification and validation testing to ensure product quality and integrity.
  • Coordination with the Success and Support teams for troubleshooting assistance and/or clinic setup.
  • Sharing feedback with the Product Manager and engineering team.
  • Documentation generation for product-related materials.
  • Medical Device documentation preparation, in cooperation with our Regulatory team, including defining requirement specifications, outlining testing conditions, executing and documenting testing, and outlining and mitigating software risks.

Required Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of experience as a Clinical Medical Physicist.
  • Validation and verification experience.
  • Programming experience using C#.
  • Strong critical thinking skills.
  • Exceptional communication skills.
  • Ability to multitask and work independently.
  • Positive attitude and a passion for excellence in patient care.
  • Detailed documentation skills, including the ability to clearly define ideas.
  • Experience with implementation of AAPM Task Group reports related to second-check systems.

Preferred Experience

  • More than 5 years of experience as a Clinical Medical Physicist.
  • Experience using Radformation products, particularly ClearCalc.
  • Experience using Visual Studio or similar coding software.
  • Familiarity with multiple treatment planning systems.
  • Product testing and/or verification experience.
  • Customer service experience.

AI & Hiring Integrity

At Radformation we believe AI can be an incredible tool for innovation, but our hiring process is all about getting to know you, your skills, experience, and unique approach to problem solving. We ask that all interviews and assessments be completed without tools that generate answers in real time. This helps ensure a fair process for everyone and allows us to see your authentic work. Using such tools during the process may affect your candidacy.

Benefits & Perks — What Makes Us RAD

We care about our people as much as we care about our mission. We offer competitive compensation, benefits, and the opportunity to make an impact in the fight against cancer. The salary range for this role is $170,000–$200,000 USD base salary plus bonus eligibility.

For US teammates (via TriNet)

Health & Wellness

  • Multiple high-quality medical plan options with substantial employer contributions toward premiums, often covering the full cost depending on the plan selected.
  • Health coverage starting on day one.
  • Short-term and long-term disability and supplementary life insurance.

Financial & Professional Growth

  • 401(k) with employer match vested immediately.
  • Annual reimbursement for professional memberships.
  • Conference attendance and continued learning opportunities.

Work-Life Balance & Perks

  • Self-managed PTO and 10 paid holidays.
  • Monthly internet stipend.
  • Company-issued laptop and one-time home office setup stipend.
  • Fully remote work environment with virtual events and yearly retreats, because we like to have fun while doing work that matters.

For global teammates (via Deel)

At Radformation, we want every team member to feel supported, no matter where they live. For teammates outside the US, we provide benefits that align with local laws and standards, working with our Employer of Record (EOR) partners to ensure fairness and equity. This means your benefits package will be locally compliant, competitive, and designed to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

Our Commitment to Diversity

Cancer affects people from every walk of life, and we believe our team should reflect that diversity. Radformation is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees.

Agency & Candidate Safety Notice

Radformation does not accept unsolicited resumes from agencies without a signed agreement in place. We do not partner with third-party recruiters unless explicitly stated. All legitimate communication from Radformation will come from an @radformation.com email address. If you receive outreach from another domain or via unofficial channels, please contact careers@radformation.com.

raw.title: Strategic Finance Senior Manager
raw.excerpt: As Marqeta’s Strategic Finance Senior Manager you will join Marqeta's FP&A team.
raw.description:
As Marqeta’s Strategic Finance Senior Manager you will join Marqeta's FP&A team. This role sits at the center of the most consequential financial questions the company is asking — cross-functional strategic initiatives, long-range planning, resource allocation, investment trade-offs, and product profitability — and partners directly with FP&A leadership to answer them.

This is a Strategic Finance role in the truest sense. The work isn't structured around the close calendar — that's the planning team's mandate. You'll certainly have recurring cadences: board-meeting analysis, leadership reviews, planning cycles. But most of your week looks like working through a portfolio of strategic projects that shape real decisions. One week you might be modeling marketing LTV to test whether a proposed budget increase actually pencils out. Next, you're partnering with the credit team on a build-versus-partner analysis for a new product. The week after, you're stress-testing a long-range scenario for an upcoming board meeting. Some projects span months; others resolve in a few days. The throughline is that good financial thinking shapes the decision.

You'll also work closely with the VP, FP&A as a trusted partner — running projects independently, representing FP&A in rooms when needed, and absorbing scope as the function grows. This is a player-coach role from day one: while it starts as an individual contributor, you'll set the bar for analytical quality across the broader team, mentor analysts informally, and grow into formal people management as the team scales.

You'll partner directly with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Operations leadership — embedded enough to understand what each team is actually trying to do, financial enough to translate that into models and recommendations, and senior enough to push back when the numbers don't support the narrative. The work spans the full P&L: topline modeling (revenue, gross profit, unit economics) and operating expense (headcount, marketing investment, T&E, vendor spend, capex). Most Strategic Finance roles skew one way or the other — this one expects fluency across both.

The pace at Marqeta is fast, the executive visibility is high, and the work is genuinely interesting. The right person is energized by ambiguity, takes pride in a clean model, and gets excited about helping operators make better decisions.

We work Flexible First. This role can be performed remotely anywhere within the U.S. or from our local Oakland office. We'd love for you to join us!

The Impact You'll Have

  • Lead cross-functional strategic projects end-to-end — from problem framing through analysis to executive recommendation. Some projects run for months, others land and resolve in two weeks
  • Build the financial models that underpin the company's biggest decisions — long-range plans, investment cases, product P&L architecture, scenario analyses for executive and board conversations
  • Partner with Sales leadership on topline strategy: bookings models, customer cohort economics, segment profitability, productivity assumptions — bringing financial rigor to the GTM conversation
  • Partner with Marketing on demand generation ROI, channel investment trade-offs, and how marketing spend connects to pipeline and bookings outcomes
  • Partner with Product and Operations leaders on opex management — building visibility into headcount investment, vendor spend, T&E, and capex against the financial plan
  • Drive deep-dive analyses that surface what the numbers are actually telling us — and translate those findings into recommendations that operators can act on
  • Build ROI frameworks the company can use to evaluate investment trade-offs consistently — across hires, programs, products, and initiatives
  • Prepare executive and board-level materials that distill complex analyses into clear narratives on company performance, strategic options, and trade-offs
  • Act as a trusted deputy to the VP of FP&A — running projects independently, representing the function in cross-functional conversations, and absorbing scope as the function grows
  • Set the bar for analytical quality across the team — mentoring analysts informally from day one, and growing into formal people management as the team expands
  • Experiment with AI to make Strategic Finance work faster and better — building modeling tools, automating recurring analyses, and finding leverage that scales judgment across more projects

Who You Are

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field — Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Math, or any discipline that built your numerical fluency
  • 7-10 years of progressive experience in Strategic Finance, FP&A, or related roles — ideally at a fintech, SaaS, or other high-growth operating company
  • An exceptional financial modeler. Mastery of Excel and Google Sheets, with comfort in SQL (or willingness to deepen those skills quickly). You build models that are clean, defensible, and actually usable by other people — not just impressive-looking to a reviewer
  • Fluent across the full P&L. You're equally comfortable modeling topline (revenue, gross profit, unit economics) and operating expense (headcount, marketing, T&E, capex). You understand how the two connect and how to make trade-offs between them
  • A track record of operating autonomously. You define problems, structure analyses, and drive to outcomes without clear precedent or a defined playbook
  • A proven cross-functional project leader. Experience leading projects with multiple cross-functional partners in fast-paced environments. You can hold several workstreams in your head at once, prioritize ruthlessly, and deliver against commitments
  • A genuine business partner. You've worked hand-in-hand with Sales and Marketing leaders before. You ask sharp questions, you bring solutions and not just problems, and you build trust by being useful — not by being agreeable
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders through crisp storytelling and data-driven recommendations. You leave executives with a clearer view of the question than they walked in with
  • A leadership mindset with the ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on execution. You're excited to do the work yourself AND set the bar for analysts around you. You're hungry to grow into formal leadership as the team scales
  • AI-curious and hungry to experiment. You already use AI tools in your day-to-day work, you have opinions about what's overhyped and what's actually useful, and you see AI as leverage to do more — not a threat or a checkbox

Nice-To-Haves

  • Experience in payments, fintech, or scaled SaaS
  • Prior experience as a trusted deputy or right-hand to a finance leader
  • Background that includes investment banking, management consulting, or equity research before moving into an operating role
  • Hands-on experience with financial planning systems (Adaptive, Anaplan, Pigment) and ERP systems (NetSuite, Workday)
  • Hands-on experience building workflows or tools with AI (custom GPTs, agents, automations, prompt engineering for finance use cases)

Compensation and Benefits

Marqeta is a Flex First company which allows you to choose your best working environment, whether that be from home or at a company office. To support Flex First, we calibrate pay to a competitive value according to working location. Compensation is aligned according to three tiers within the United States:

  • National: A baseline tier that applies to most of the geographic territory of the United States.
  • Premium: Slightly elevated from the National tier, and oriented toward a narrower set of higher cost-of-living areas, such as Los Angeles CA and Seattle WA
  • Premium Plus: A tier for the most expensive working areas, like the San Francisco Bay area and New York City.

Visit this page or consult with a Recruiter to determine which tier would be applicable to you.

When determining salaries, we consider several factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior experience, and work location. The new-hire base salary range for this position is:

  • National: $156,000 - $195,000
  • Premium: $165,500 - $206,900
  • Premium Plus: 175,000 - $218,800

We also believe in recognizing the contributions of our people. That's why we award annual bonuses to eligible employees, rewarding both individual performance and the success of the entire company.

Along with monetary compensation, Marqeta offers

  • Multiple health insurance options
  • Flexible time off – take what you need
  • Retirement savings program with company contribution and after tax contributions
  • Equity in a publicly-traded company and an Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Family-forming benefits, fertility support, and up to 20 weeks of Parental Leave
  • Free therapy sessions, financial and professional coaching, and legal advice
  • Monthly stipend to support our remote work model
  • Annual “development dollars” to support our people growth and development
  • Through Flex First, the freedom to live and work wherever you and your family thrive
